title: Pistachio Ice Cream
subtitle: Custard-based ice cream with a pistachio paste blended through
excerpt: A rich custard ice cream with a dense, oily pistachio paste worked through the base, the result is an intensely nutty, pale green ice cream with a flavour that is nothing like the artificial versions.
sourceNotes: Pistachio gelato is a Sicilian classic, widely credited to Bronte in the Catania region, which produces some of the world's finest pistachios. The British ice cream version, built on a crème anglaise rather than a gelato base, began appearing in UK recipe books in the late 1990s and is now a regular feature of artisan British ice cream makers.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Press baking paper against the surface.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The custard and pistachio paste can be prepared the day before and the base assembled, then churned the following day.

content.text: Pistachio ice cream is a custard base with pistachio paste blended through before churning. The paste takes 3 to 4 minutes in a food processor to go from chopped nuts to a smooth, spreadable consistency. Use unsalted, unroasted pistachios for the cleanest flavour.

items.prepNote: unsalted, shelled, blitz to a smooth paste in a food processor with 1 tbsp of the sugar
reserve 1 tbsp for the pistachio paste

content.text: Put the pistachios and 1 tablespoon of caster sugar in a food processor and blitz for 3 to 4 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides every minute. The nuts will go through a rough crumb stage before gradually releasing their oils and becoming a smooth, slightly tacky paste. This takes longer than it seems, be patient and continue until the paste is smooth rather than just finely ground.

Whisk the egg yolks with the remaining caster sugar in a large heatproof bowl until pale and thick. Combine the milk and double cream in a medium saucepan and heat to just below boiling. Pour the hot cream mixture slowly onto the yolks, whisking constantly, then return to the saucepan over a low heat. Stir for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Remove from the heat and whisk in the pistachio paste, vanilla extract, and almond extract if using, until fully combined. The custard will turn pale green. Pour through a sieve into a clean bowl, press cling film onto the surface, and cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Churn the cold custard in an ice cream maker for 25 minutes until thick and softly set. Transfer to a freezer-safe container, seal, and freeze for at least 6 hours or overnight.

items.symptom: Pistachio paste is still grainy after blitzing
items.cause: The nuts have not released enough oil, or the food processor is not powerful enough.
items.fix: Add 1 teaspoon of neutral oil (such as sunflower) to help the paste come together. Continue blitzing in longer bursts. A slightly grainy paste will not ruin the ice cream but will give a less smooth texture.

items.symptom: Custard turned too grainy when the paste was added
items.cause: The paste was added when the custard was still hot enough to cause the nut oils to separate.
items.fix: Let the custard cool slightly off the heat, about 65°C, before whisking in the paste. Whisk vigorously to emulsify the oils.

items.cause: The pistachios were not fresh, or the paste was too small a quantity for the custard base.
items.fix: Use the freshest pistachios available, stale nuts have almost no flavour. Increase to 175g next time for a more pronounced result.

content.text: Keeps in the freezer for up to 3 months. Remove from the freezer 5 minutes before scooping. The colour fades slightly over time but the flavour remains good.
